The Chief Executive
has approved that: 
 

1. 
Bloom Procurement Services Limited be directly awarded a
contract via the NEPRO3 Framework which is a fully compliant
procurement framework which assists the UK public sector to buy and
manage specialist professional services from a choice of
regional and national suppliers. Bloom Procurement Services
are the UK’s exclusive operator of the NEPRO solution,
on behalf of NEPO (the North East Procurement Organisation) –
20 categories are available through the NEPRO3 solution –
this appointment relates to Project and Cost Management for Project
Management and Cost Consultant Services at a cost of £188,000
for the purpose of developing detailed proposals for the creation
of a permanent outdoor market square within Central Birkenhead with
covered stalls, public realm improvements and flexible space
capable of accommodating a range of market and event activities;
and 

 

2. 
the services be delivered by Simon Fenton Partnership LLP as sub-
contractor to Bloom Procurement Services Limited with an associated
collateral contract in favour of the Council.

On 18 November 2025,
the Council’s Economy, Regeneration and Housing Committee
resolved to approve, in principle, a phased approach to the future
of Birkenhead Market, including: 
 

Phase 1- the
relocation of market traders into refurbished units within
Birkenhead Town Centre and the demolition of the existing market
building; and 

 

Phase 2- the
development of proposals for the creation of a permanent outdoor
market square with covered stalls, public realm improvements and
flexible space capable of accommodating a range of market and event
activities. 

 
The Committee further
resolved that additional work should be undertaken to develop
proposals for Phase 2 and that a further report should be brought
to Committee regarding the future use and design of the land
vacated by the current market site. 
 
The appointment of a
Project Manager and Cost Consultant is required to develop
proposals for Phase 2. 
 
The appointment will
provide the specialist expertise needed to develop and assess Phase
2 proposals for the Birkenhead Market site. 
 
The appointment will
enable the Council to develop a comprehensive vision and design for
a new market square and public realm space, establish
deliverability and cost parameters, undertake stakeholder
engagement and prepare a future decision-making report for
Members. 
 
The scheme is funded
by the Ministry of Housing Communities and Local Government, Local
Regeneration Fund. 
 
The commission will
support the Council's wider regeneration ambitions for Birkenhead
Town Centre and ensure proposals align with the objectives of the
Birkenhead 2040 Framework.

An alternative option
would be for the Council to seek to develop Phase 2 proposals
solely through existing internal resources. This option is not
recommended because the work requires specialist expertise due to
the breadth and complexity of the commission.

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Chief Executive is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

purpose:
This report seeks approval for a phased
modernisation of adult day services in Wirral, aligning provision
with national policy and local ambitions to promote independence,
wellbeing and community inclusion. The proposals would gradually
move from a predominantly building-based model towards more
personalised day opportunities, while retaining specialist support
for people with complex needs.

content:
The Interim Director
of Capital Programmes has approved the award of a contract to Pool
Technical Services Limited (Company Number 07967122) as the most
advantageous tender for a period of 2-years with an option to
extend for a further year to provide pool plant specialist services
for Wirral Council’s Active Wirral Services within five
Council owned leisure centres with an estimated contract value of
£240,000 over a period of three years.
 

Active Wirral operates
five leisure centres containing seven swimming pools that are
heavily used by residents across the borough. The pool programmes
cover learn?to?swim provision, school swimming, public swimming and
competitive club activity. These facilities rely on a complex pool
plant system that requires year?round maintenance. Much of the
plant equipment is ageing and increasingly prone to failure.
 
The specialist will
become the single point of contact (POC) for Facilities Management
in order for Active Wirral to maintain the complex pool plant
operation and remain compliant within the boundaries of Health and
safety.
 
Historically, Active
Wirral relied on six different suppliers to respond when equipment
broke down. Following the transfer of reporting, management and
budget responsibilities to the Corporate Landlord, officers
concluded that the existing multi?supplier approach was too complex
for the central team to manage effectively. To ensure the correct
specialists could be deployed quickly and consistently, a decision
was made to tender for a single pool?plant contractor to work
alongside Facilities Management and support the integration of
plant assets into Concerto.
 
A detailed scope,
specification and pricing document for the required service was
issued in April 2026 to eight suppliers and a tender exercise
undertaken. Five bids were received, including from Pool Technical
Services. They were evaluated on price, quality and social value
submissions and moderated with the Council’s Procurement
Team. Details of the tender evaluation are set out in the exempt
Appendix 1.
 
Appendix 1 is exempt
from publication pursuant to paragraph 3 of part 1 of Schedule 12 A
of the Local Government Act 1972 (Information relating to the
financial or business affairs of any particular person (including
the authority holding that information)) because it contains or
refers to information relating to the financial and business
affairs of tenderers and the Council and the public interest in
maintaining the exemption outweighs the public interest in
disclosure.
 
The evaluation
criteria was based on price (50%), quality (40%) and social value
(10%).
 
Quality elements of
the tender return were evaluated by two officers from the Asset
Management team and one officer from Neighbourhoods team,
completing individual scoring sheets which were moderated by
Procurement.
 
The Pricing element of
the tender return was scored separately by the Procurement team
 
The final scores were
brought together by the Procurement team in a weighted "evaluation
matrix" which determined the preferred tenderer. The tender
submitted by Pool technical services represents the most
advantageous tender received.
 
Pool technical
services were successful in the tender process. The company has
worked with Active Wirral for over 20 years and has extensive
knowledge of our systems.

Do Nothing: This
option was discounted as the Council needs to have a contract in
place in order to fulfil its statutory
duty to ensure that its assets comply with relevant Health and
Safety Legislation and Regulations
 
To take no action,
leaving the Council without a tendered contractor responsible for
servicing, maintaining and reporting on the pool plant to the
Facilities Management team. Under the current arrangement, the
process is complex, and staff without specialist pool?plant
knowledge would struggle to identify the correct supplier to
contact, the reason for doing so, and the appropriate timing.
 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

The Assistant
Director: Chief Regeneration Officer has approved the appointment
of Buro Happold Limited to deliver the Liscard Regeneration
Programme – Public Realm Improvements Design Consultancy, as
the highest scoring tenderer in accordance with the most
economically advantageous tender criteria, following a mini
procurement exercise conducted under the CCS Construction
Professional Services 2: RM6356 – Lot 1: General
Infrastructure Framework, with a contract term until
31st March 2028 with a total contract cost of
£225,586. 

This
decision supports the delivery of the Liscard Regeneration
Programme.  The Council has developed an
outline (RIBA Stage 2) design for public realm improvements within
Liscard Town Centre and is now required to appoint a suitably
qualified lead design consultancy to progress the scheme through
detailed design, tender preparation, and delivery
support.
 
A
detailed specification of requirements for the required services
was issued on 22nd June 2026 to suppliers a setting out
the following requirements through a mini tendering exercise
conducted pursuant to the CCS Construction
Professional Services 2: RM6356 – Lot 1: General
Infrastructure Framework as follows:
 
· 
Develop a coordinated, technically robust and
buildable scheme through RIBA Stages 3–4;
· 
Undertake and manage required surveys,
investigations, and multidisciplinary inputs;
· 
Produce detailed tender documentation to enable
contractor procurement;
· 
 Ensure compliance with
statutory requirements, including funding requirements, and
alignment with Council standards; and
· 
Support delivery of a high-quality scheme aligned
with regeneration and placemaking objectives
 
3 bids
were received. The bids were evaluated having regard to the most
advantageous tenderer criteria as detailed in the exempt Appendix,
with the following weightings Price 30%, Quality 70% and Social
Value xx%.
 
Buro
Happold Limited was the preferred tenderer,
scoring the highest having regard to the evaluation
criteria.
 
Failure
to procure these services at this stage would delay programme
delivery and risk the Council’s ability to progress the
scheme in line with funding requirements.
 
The
cost to deliver RIBA 3 and 4 is £152,312.50. RIBA Stages 5-7
are to be delivered on time and material basis; therefore a
£50,000 provisional sum allocation is required for that
process. In addition, the following sums are required for fixed
priced surveys £15,129 / provisional sum surveys
£8,145.  The total cost to
progress the scheme through detailed design, tender preparation,
and provide delivery support is £225,586
 
The
commission will be funded via the Council’s Local
Regeneration Fund, and this funding was approved by the
Council’s Economy, Regeneration and Housing Committee on 19
January 2026.
 
Appendix 1 contains exempt information as defined in Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972. It is in the public interest
to exclude the press and public under Paragraph 3
‘Information relating to the financial or business affairs of
any particular person (including the authority holding the
information).’

Do nothing –
This option has been discounted as it would prevent progression of
the scheme beyond concept stage, delay delivery, and risk funding
and regeneration outcomes.
 
Undertake design
in-house – This option has been discounted due to the
requirement for specialist multidisciplinary expertise and capacity
not being available internally.

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

The Director of Capital
Programmes and Assets has approved
 

1. 
the surrender of the lease of 27 Princes Pavement, Birkenhead,
currently held by Cash Converters (UK) Stores Ltd (“Cash
Converters”)

 

2. 
the grant of a lease of 21 Borough Pavement, Birkenhead on
commercial terms accompanied by a landlord capital contribution
(paid by the Council) to Cash Converters (UK) Stores Ltd as set out
in the exempt appendix 1.
 

Cash
Converters (UK) Stores Ltd (“the tenant”) currently
occupies 27 Princes Pavement a unit in a row of shops which are
adjacent to the former House of Fraser site.  The retail units will need to be demolished to
allow the regeneration project for the adjacent site to
proceed.  All other units in the row are
currently vacant with the exception of
one other unit which there is facility to enable possession by the
Council, therefore the lease of 27 Princes Pavement is the only
remaining impediment to obtaining vacant possession of the row of
shops for redevelopment.
 
As the
tenant occupies on a lease which contains the security of tenure
provisions of the Landlord & Tenant Act 1954 Part II, the
tenant has a statutory right to renew the lease of its existing
premises now that it has reached contractual expiry. Therefore,
negotiations have taken place and terms
have been agreed to enable the tenant to take a new lease of an
alternative vacant unit in The Grange Shopping Centre without the
need for the Council to serve formal Notices on the tenant under
section 25 of the Landlord & Tenant Act 1954.  In accordance with market practice a landlord
(Council) capital contribution has been agreed as a contribution
towards the costs of the tenant’s fitting out works in the
new unit for the tenant’s benefit. 
The
tenant will be granted a new lease for the new unit on commercial
terms and their existing lease will be
surrendered within 6 weeks of the new lease commencing. 
 
The
granting of the new lease will retain the tenant within the
Shopping Centre which will protect rental income for the
Council.  It will also protect levels of
occupancy and footfall in the town centre, which is supportive of
the Council’s goal to help regenerate Birkenhead town centre
and encourage spend in the local economy.
 
The
detailed terms of the arrangement which is subject of this decision
is set out in the exempt Appendix 1.
 
Appendix 1 contains exempt information as defined in Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972. 
It is in the public interest to exclude the press and public under
Paragraph 3 ‘Information relating to the financial or
business affairs of any particular person (including the authority
holding the information)’.
 

One alternative option
is to ‘do nothing’ – in this scenario the tenant
may decide to leave Birkenhead town centre which will result in
reduced rental income, increased void costs and reduced
footfall. 
 
Other alternative
options are set out in exempt Appendix 2. 
 
Appendix 2 contains
exempt information as defined in Schedule 12A of the Local
Government Act 1972.  It is in the
public interest to exclude the press and public under Paragraph 3
‘Information relating to the financial or business affairs of
any particular person (including the authority holding the
information)’.
 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Director is satisfied that
paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.
 
Background

Heads of Terms
JLL Recommendation

The Director of Capital Programmes has
approved the direct award of a contract to Steer Ltd via the ESPO
Consultancy Services – Lot 5 for the provision of specialist
economic appraisal and transport assessment expertise to support
the development of the Gateway 2 submissions for the Council's
Transport for City Region (Birkenhead Central Gateway and Core
Active Travel Network projects), with a contract term of 6 months
at an estimated contract cost of £96,225 + VAT.
 

The Birkenhead Central Gateway
and Core Active Travel Network are key priorities within the
Liverpool City Region Combined Authority’s (LCRCA) Transport
for City Region (TCR) £1.6bn settlement.
 
Funding for the Birkenhead
Central Gateway and Core Active Travel Network are subject to a
structured ‘Gateway’ business case process via the
LCRCA. The Council secured conditional approval for both projects
at the first stage in the business case process (Gateway 1) in
March 2026.
 
Both projects now require the
preparation of a robust and compliant Gateway 2 Strategic Outline
Business Case to support progression through the LCRCA assurance
process. The Council has identified that
it does not have the capacity and expertise in-house to deliver Gateway 2
requirements.
The appointment of Steer Ltd
will provide specialist economic appraisal and transport assessment
expertise to support the development of
the Gateway 2 submissions, including appraisal specification,
review of existing transport modelling evidence, options assessment
and preparation of the Gateway 2 economic cases and supporting
documentation.
 
The Steer Ltd appointment will
be via ESPO Consultancy Services – Lot 5.
 
The appointment of Steer Ltd
will ensure that the Council has access to the specialist economic
and transport assessment resources required to produce a high-quality, credible and
submission-ready business case within the required programme
timescales, reducing risks to programme delivery and future funding
opportunities.
 
The cost of the Steer Ltd
commission is £96,225 + VAT.
 
The contract cost will be fully
funded via the Council’s LCRCA TCR pre-development grant
award.
 


(1) 
One option would be not
to appoint external specialist support and to prepare the Gateway 2
SOBC solely using internal resources. This option has been discounted as the business case
requires specialist programme, commercial and cost management
expertise and dedicated coordination
capacity within challenging delivery timescales.

(2) 
Another option would be
to procure the required services through
an open competitive procurement process,
however, the timescales associated with this option would impact on
the LCRCA Gateway approval deadlines and project
delivery.
 

Confirmation that the Director is satisfied
that the decision is not reserved to a committee (paragraphs 2(a)
to 2(c) of the Overview and Scheme of Delegations of Authority to
Officers.)

Submission)
 
Core Active Travel Network (Gateway 1
Submission)

The Director of
Corporate Services has approved the direct award of a contract
via the Y23038 Framework for Supply of ICT Managed Services
and Consultancy under Lot 2 to Phoenix Software Limited with effect
from 21st July 2026 for ICT Consultancy Services for a period of
one year at a total cost of £408000.
 

The objective of the
Technology Transformation Programme is to remove the
Council’s reliance on ageing infrastructure by moving to a
modern, cloud
based hosting arrangement. This change is required to reduce
infrastructure risk and ensure the continued reliability of
critical services used by residents and staff.
 
Moving from legacy
data centre infrastructure to the cloud is a business-critical
activity that must be carefully managed to protect service
continuity and sensitive information. An experienced delivery
partner is required to support this work. The proposed partner has
a proven track record of successfully delivering similar cloud
migrations and understands the governance, service pressures and
risks involved in local government environments, alongside adoption
and optimisation opportunities. This provides confidence that the
transition can be delivered safely and efficiently using proven
methods.
 
The engagement will
include structured handover and training for Council staff,
ensuring teams are able to support and manage the system following
migration.
 

Do nothing. This was
discounted as the Council has a requirement for migration of
on-premises infrastructure to Cloud due to end of life.
 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Director is satisfied that
paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

approved the award of a contract to Vivedia Limited following an
open tender process for the provision of music, webcasting, and
visual tribute services within Wirral Cemeteries and Landican
Crematorium for a period of 3 years with the option to extend for
up to two additional years in annual increments with effect from 19
January 2026 at a total contract value of £208,677.17.
 

This contract is required to ensure the
continued provision of high-quality, sensitive, and accessible
bereavement services to families and funeral directors across
Wirral.

tributes, and webcasting, are integral to delivering personalised
and inclusive funeral experiences.

accordance with the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules,
ensuring compliance, transparency, and best value. Two bids were
received and evaluated against the following criteria:

Quality – 40%
Price – 50%
Social Value – 10%

 
Vivedia (Obitus) achieved the highest overall
score and demonstrated the necessary specialist expertise and
sector experience to deliver this service effectively.

An in-house provision was considered; however,

tribute, and webcasting services.

the procurement exercise, with Vivedia (Obitus) scoring highest

The Interim Director of Operations has
approved the direct award of a contract using the YPO Framework
001032 (Crematoria Solutions III) Lot 2 – Maintenance, to
IFZW Maintenance Ltd for the maintenance of two KE400 freefall
cremators and associated abatement and cremation equipment at
Landican Crematorium, with effect from 1 January 2026 at a total
contract value of £416,500.00.
 

The contract is required to ensure ongoing
statutory compliance, adherence to environmental legislation, and
health and safety standards, enabling the continued operation of
Landican Crematorium, Wirral’s only crematorium, which
undertakes between 3,000 and 3,200 cremations per annum.
 
The KE400 and KE400+ cremators are freefall
units, installed and commissioned in November 2011, and are of a
unique design not used elsewhere in the UK. IFZW are the original
equipment manufacturer and installer, and their specialist
technical knowledge ensures maintenance is completed to the highest
manufacturer standards, safeguarding equipment integrity,
longevity, and service continuity.
 
This arrangement includes maintenance
provision through to 2029 and the relining of cremator No. 1 during
summer 2026, representing excellent value for money, with
refractory brickwork achieving a lifespan of approximately 15
years.
 
A further competition was undertaken via The
Chest under the YPO Framework in accordance with Contract Procedure
Rules. One compliant bid was received and evaluated on:

Quality – 50%
Price – 40%
Social Value – 10%

 
The bid submitted by IFZW Maintenance Ltd
achieved the highest overall score, falls within the approved
budget, and represents best value.
 

The Council does not possess the in house
technical expertise to safely maintain freefall cremators of this
specialist design.
 
Due to the niche nature of cremator
manufacture and refractory brickwork, together with proprietary
operating software, alternative suppliers would be unlikely to
demonstrate the required specialist
capability or quality standards.
 
Use of non specialist contractors would present
unacceptable operational, safety, environmental, and compliance
risks to service delivery.

The Director is satisfied that the decision is
not reserved to a committee (paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) of the
Overview and Scheme of Delegations of Authority to Officers.)

• Undertake and

inputs;
• Produce
detailed tender documentation to enable contractor procurement;
• Ensure
compliance with statutory requirements, including funding
requirements, and alignment with Council standards; and
• Support
delivery of a high-quality scheme aligned with regeneration and
placemaking objectives
 
The commission will be
funded via the Council’s Local Regeneration Fund, which was
approved by the Council’s Economy, Regeneration and Housing
Committee on 19 January 2026 . The

expertise and capacity not being available internally.

That the Director of
Capital Programmes and Assets be authorised to appoint Corstorphine
and Wright to oversee the specification for works for vacant space
with the Mallory and Irvine Buildings.

The Mallory and Irvine
Buildings were constructed to support the regeneration of
Birkenhead Town Centre either through occupation by Council staff,
letting to a commercial occupier, or a combination of the
two.  In line with the details set out
in the report, the Council will need to fit out some of the
currently vacant space to accommodate staff.
 
The commercial
sub-letting of the Birkenhead Commercial District (BCD) is part of
the rationale behind the development of these assets, generating
footfall, vibrancy and other benefits. Letting the assets will
bring in income which the Council needs to support the rent it
needs to pay for the assets. Fitting out the assets is an essential
step in enabling them to be fully let.
 

The Council has
considered a number of options for these buildings which revolve
around whether occupation is by the Council, commercial letting to
third parties or a combination of the two.  This has been dictated to some degree by the
ability to let the space on suitably commercial terms.  The current position is considered to be the best
achievable at this time.

decision_maker: Children Young People and Education Committee
content:
Kelsey Goodwin asked
what procedures were in place to ensure that correspondence with
parents was responded to in a timely, accurate and compliant with
the SEND code of practice.
 
The Chair responded
Wirral Children’s Services had made significant investment
over the previous 18 months to strengthen SEND provision,
particularly within the SENDSTART Team. This had helped address
longstanding concerns about delays in communication and issuing
Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs), with schools and families
reporting improved support.
 
There had been
measurable progress, including a reduction in outstanding EHC
assessments from 657 in May 2025 to 271 by April 2026. However,
demand remained high, with a 20% increase in EHCPs since early 2025
and around 140 new assessment requests each month. As a result, the
service was not yet consistently meeting statutory timescales or
quality expectations.
Robust processes were
in place to manage complaints and delays, with issues escalated,
monitored, and used to inform improvement, including learning from
Ombudsman findings.
 
He noted that
communication had also improved, with greater transparency through
regular reporting, the SEND Local Offer website, and updates shared
via social media and partner organisations to keep families
informed.
 
Kelsey questioned how,
despite claims of robust processes, a parent received written
confirmation from NICE that clinical guidelines cited by officers
did not exist. These guidelines were reportedly used to justify
reversing an agreement after the authority had already acknowledged
a prolonged failure to meet Section F provision.
 
The situation was
described as particularly concerning because the disputed guidance
was issued during a child’s GCSE period, potentially causing
further educational harm. She highlighted the discrepancy,
prompting concerns that incorrect information may go unchallenged
by others without such expertise.
 
The Chair responded
that Kelsey would receive written response within 10 working
days.
 
Kelsey asked that the
response be copied to Angela Eagle MP.
topline: The Children Young People and Education Committee has decided to approve recommendations for improving communication and SEND provision, despite ongoing challenges.

content:
The
Director of Capital Programmes has approved the grant of a new
lease, surrender of an existing lease and completion of any further
legal documentation to enable the relocation of an existing tenant
(‘The Tenant’) on the terms set out in this report and
exempt appendix 1.
 
 

In 2023 the Council purchased the Pyramids and
Grange Shopping Centre from the Mars Pension Fund Trustees. The
shopping centre is the primary retail core of Birkenhead. It has
been in a state of decline over the last decade with the growth of
online retailing, accelerated by the Covid pandemic. This led to
significant vacancy within the centre. The Council’s actions
in respect to seeking to regenerate Birkenhead town centre are
aimed at activation of the high street to stimulate new retail,
leisure and other commercial uses to encourage investment and spend
in the local economy.
 
JLL in its role as Investment Manager has been
working with the letting agents (Barker Proudlove and Emanuel
Oliver) to maximise occupation through new lettings and tenant
retention wherever possible, taking account of the Council’s
regeneration ambitions.
 
The Tenant is currently ‘holding
over’ on their existing lease. JLL and the appointed letting
agents have negotiated a set of Heads of Terms on behalf of the
Council for the relocation of The Tenant which will take a new
lease on the relocation unit and surrender their existing lease as
set out in the exempt Appendix 1. It has been agreed that the
Tenant will take on responsibility for these works on the basis
that the Landlord will reimburse the cost of undertaking these
works.
 
Proceeding with the relocation without further
delay is important to provide The Tenant opportunity to complete
its relocation prior to the Christmas trading period towards the
end of 2026, and the new lease will provide certainty over their
occupation within the town centre for the foreseeable future. The
Tenant is a national retailer with strong financial standing and
plays a key role in supporting footfall and vibrancy within
Birkenhead town centre.
 
Relocation will retain The Tenant within
Birkenhead and will secure occupation of a unit which is vacant
since 2018, providing a modern fit-out, reducing ongoing void costs
and improving the overall perception of the shopping centre
environment.
 
Allowing the Tenant to carry out the Landlord
Enabling Works (which are required for any future letting of the
unit) will reduce the risk of delays, help avoid extra costs for
the Council and support The Tenant moving into the unit on
time.
 
The detailed terms of the arrangement which is
subject of this decision is set out in the exempt Appendix 1.
 
Appendix 1 contains
exempt information as defined in Schedule 12A of the Local
Government Act 1972.  It is in the
public interest to exclude the press and public under Paragraph 3
‘Information relating to the financial or business affairs of
any particular person (including the authority holding the
information)’.

The ‘do
nothing’ option would likely result in The Tenant exiting
Birkenhead completely, as the Tenant has stated that it does not
wish to remain in its existing unit. This would add another empty
unit to the town centre resulting in additional costs incurred
while the property is vacant and impacting the perception of the
vibrancy of the town centre. 
 
The Council could
continue to market the vacant relocation unit in the open market to
seek an alternative tenant, however the space has been marketed
since 2018 with limited interest. A letting to a different tenant
might leave Council responsible for the annual void costs.
Additionally, a letting would not be possible given the vacant
unit’s current condition and configuration, and so the cost
of the Landlord Enabling Works would need to be incurred at a
future date to facilitate any letting and that would be subject to
further cost inflation. 
 
Council-led delivery
of the Landlord Enabling Works to the vacant relocation unit was
rejected due to procurement complexity, delays before work could
begin, increased cost risk and additional project management
costs.
 
The relocation unit is
not currently in a lettable condition. One option discussed was for
the Council to undertake an agreed set of Landlord’s Enabling
Works, prior to the Tenant taking possession, however due to
potential issues, timings and delays with some of the elements
(including asbestos/boiler removal and the works to the goods lift)
this option was rejected.

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Director is satisfied that
paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

JLL Recommendation

This report recommends
the variation of a contract with Wirral Community Health and Care
NHS Foundation Trust for the delivery of the Healthy Child
programme, using the Public Health Grant to the total additional
sum of £636,974 for the period April 2026 to January 2027.
The funding will meet the recurrent staffing cost pressures arising
from nationally confirmed NHS Agenda for Change pay uplifts for
2026/27, set at 3.3%.
 

The Director of Public
Health has decided to approve a contract variation with Wirral
Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust for the delivery of
the Healthy Child programme to meet the nationally agreed NHS
Agenda for Change staff pay awards for the period 1 April 2026 to
31 January 2027 for the total additional sum of £636,974.
 

Public Health
commissions a number of services from
Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust, to deliver
both mandated and non-mandated Public Health services.
Responsibility for paying the nationally agreed NHS staff
inflationary uplifts for Public Health contracts (for staff
directly employed to deliver these services) has transferred to
Local Authorities (Public Health budgets) from NHS Cheshire &
Merseyside Integrated Care Board (ICB), to account for pay awards
from 1st April 2023.
 
The recommendation
ensures continuity of a critical statutory service, mitigates risks
to safeguarding public health outcomes for children and families,
and addresses identified funding gaps in direct staffing costs
following nationally determined NHS pay uplifts.
 

Alternative options
considered include not awarding any additional funding beyond the
agreed agenda for change pay uplift, however the outcome to this
would result in high risk of significant service disruption,
provider withdrawal, and breach of Council statutory
duties.  Alternative providers are
limited, and emergency arrangements would likely incur higher costs
and destabilise other key services for children and families
locally.  Therefore, this option was not
deemed appropriate.
 
Alternative options to
mitigate the impact of financial pressures within the service would
have a direct impact on the quality and effectiveness of the
contract, including statutory functions, therefore this option was
not deemed appropriate.

content:
The Assistant Director
-Chief Planning Officer has approved:
the Birkenhead Park Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Plan
as set out in Appendix 3.

Section 69(1) of the
Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 (the
Act) requires the Council to from time to time determine which
parts of its areas of special architectural or historic interest
the character or appearance of which it is desirable to preserve or
enhance, and designate those areas as conservation areas.
Section 69(2) of the Act requires the Council from time to time to
review the past exercise of functions under this section and to
determine whether any parts or any further parts of its area should
be designated as conservation areas and, if it so determines, it
shall designate those parts accordingly.

The Act requires the review, and protection of Conservation
Areas.

The Birkenhead Park Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Plan
outlines the way in which the Council will seek to preserve or
enhance the relevant area and how it will monitor its activities in
this regard. The plan also presents several regeneration proposals
which will help improve the quality of the area.

The Birkenhead Park Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Plan
was subject to a 6-week public consultation period, commencing on
30th June 2025, including events held for the local community on
4th July 2025 at Birkenhead Park Visitor Centre. All properties
within the conservation area were notified by letter.

An analysis of the consultation responses and the day long
community event and officer response has been carried out and is
set out as Appendix 1. 47 comments were received, with 46 responses
through the online portal and 1 paper copy. Several amendments have
been made to the appraisal as a result of the consultation and
community event.

It has been decided to approve the Birkenhead Park Conservation
Area Appraisal and Management Plan (as set out in Appendix 3 to
this report). This will replace the old plan approved in 2007. The
adoption of the Birkenhead Park Conservation Area Appraisal and
Management Plan will serve as a material consideration in the
determination of relevant planning applications and enforcement
decisions.

purpose:
DECISION
 
The Director of Corporate
Services  has approved the award of a
concession contract and lease to Coastal WK LTD for the operation
of the West Kirby Marine Lake and Wirral Watersports Centre,
following a fully compliant procurement process undertaken in
accordance with the Council’s Contract Procedure
Rules.  The  contract and lease will be awarded for an
initial term of five years, with an option to extend for a further
five years, alongside a ten?year lease agreement incorporating a
mutual break clause exercisable at the fifth anniversary. Estimated
contract value information in set out in Appendix B (restricted
enclosure).
 
 
 
REASONS FOR THE DECISION
 
Financial sustainability and budget savings
The current operating model
requires an ongoing revenue subsidy from the Council and exposes it
to future operating, repair and maintenance costs. Outsourcing the
operation will remove these costs, delivering an annual revenue
saving while also generating concession income over the 10?year
contract term. This directly supports approved budget savings and
reduces long?term financial exposure.
 
Risk
transfer and asset protection
The proposed arrangement
transfers day?to?day operational responsibility, staffing, and
routine maintenance liabilities to an external specialist operator,
reducing the Council’s financial and operational risk. This
approach provides greater certainty over future expenditure while
ensuring the asset is managed and maintained appropriately,
safeguarding its long?term condition and value (excluding Marine
Lake responsibilities where these are retained).
 
Continuation and enhancement of service provision
The appointment secures the
continued delivery of core watersports provision at the site,
ensuring ongoing public access to activities and learning
opportunities. An external operator with relevant expertise is
better placed to grow participation, develop programming, and
maximise usage of the facility.
 
Support for long?term viability of the site
By removing the requirement for
an ongoing subsidy and aligning costs with income generation, the
proposed model establishes a more sustainable footing for the
Watersports Centre and Marine Lake. This increases resilience to
future financial pressures and supports the continued operation of
the asset as an important community facility.
 
Alignment to Council strategic objectives
The proposal aligns with the
Council’s wider objectives to under the Medium Term Financial
Strategy (MTFS) to deliver a balanced budget and sustainable
council, to encourage partnership working with external operators,
and protect key community assets while managing financial risk
responsibly.
 
OTHER
OPTIONS CONSIDERED
Other options considered were
to:
 
a) 
Do Nothing – Continue with a Wirral Council
owned and operated Watersports operation. This option was rejected
as it would not deliver the agreed budget savings and would not
support the Council’s strategic objective of achieving a
balanced and sustainable financial position.
 
b) 
Only lease or outsource distinct parts of the asset,
primarily, vacant space, previously occupied by the  former Sail Loft cafe. 
This was presented to the market but received limited expressions
of interest due to concerns around multiple tenants occupying space
within the building.
 
c) 
Cease activity at the site, mothball the facility
and withdraw from the delivery of watersports. This option was
discounted for multiple reasons. The Wirral Watersports Centre is
considered as a premier destination in the North of England for
many wind-based watersports including windsurfing and wingfoiling.
The centre also supports a range of other water based activities
and is used by the private West Kirby Sailing Club. Access to
watersports, coastal activity and open space is a key component of
the Councils Sports & Physical Activity Strategy. The site is
an important, cherished destination in the heart of West Kirby and
has significant potential to increase tourism in the local
area.

Watersports Centre and Marine Lake. This increases resilience to
future financial pressures and supports the continued operation of
the asset as an important community facility.
 
Alignment to Council strategic objectives
The proposal aligns with the
Council’s wider objectives to under the Medium Term Financial
Strategy (MTFS) to deliver a balanced budget and sustainable
council, to encourage partnership working with external operators,
and protect key community assets while managing financial risk
responsibly.
 
OTHER
OPTIONS CONSIDERED
Other options considered were
to:
 
a) 
Do Nothing – Continue with a Wirral Council
owned and operated Watersports operation. This option was rejected
as it would not deliver the agreed budget savings and would not
support the Council’s strategic objective of achieving a
balanced and sustainable financial position.
 
b) 
Only lease or outsource distinct parts of the asset,
primarily, vacant space, previously occupied by the  former Sail Loft cafe. 
This was presented to the market but received limited expressions
of interest due to concerns around multiple tenants occupying space
within the building.
 
c) 
Cease activity at the site, mothball the facility
and withdraw from the delivery of watersports. This option was
discounted for multiple reasons. The Wirral Watersports Centre is
considered as a premier destination in the North of England for
many wind-based watersports including windsurfing and wingfoiling.
The centre also supports a range of other water based activities
and is used by the private West Kirby Sailing Club. Access to
watersports, coastal activity and open space is a key component of
the Councils Sports & Physical Activity Strategy. The site is
an important, cherished destination in the heart of West Kirby and
has significant potential to increase tourism in the local
area. 
 

The Director of Corporate Services has
approved the award of a concession contract and lease to Coastal WK
LTD for the operation of the West Kirby Marine Lake and Wirral
Watersports Centre, following a fully compliant procurement process
undertaken in accordance with the Council’s Contract
Procedure Rules.  The  contract and lease will be awarded for an
initial term of five years, with an option to extend for a further
five years, alongside a ten?year lease agreement incorporating a
mutual break clause exercisable at the fifth anniversary. Estimated
contract value information in set out in Appendix B (restricted
enclosure).

content:
The Assistant Director
of Property and Investment has approved the award of a contract,
the Water Hygiene Monitoring and Risk Assessment Contract, for a
period of 2 years with the option to extend for a further year on
two occasions, commencing 1st June 2026, to HSL
Compliance Ltd (Company Number 02425951) as the Most Economically
Advantageous Tenderer pursuant to a mini competition conducted via
Lot 10 (Surveys, Testing and Treatments) of the Yorkshire
Purchasing Organisation Dynamic Procurement System 882 (Building
Internal Fit-out and Maintenance). The scope of the contract is for
the provision of water hygiene monitoring and risk assessment
services in relation to the Council's land and property with an
estimated contract value of £600,000 over a period of four
years.
 

The Council manages an
extensive portfolio of properties, many of which contain water
systems that require regular monitoring and testing. To ensure
compliance with the Approved Code of Practice L8 –
Legionnaires’ Disease: The Control of Legionella Bacteria in
Water Systems – the Council must carry out monthly
inspections, water sampling, and statutory servicing of
thermostatic mixing valves. Establishing the means to appoint
qualified contractors to perform these essential tasks is a
critical step in maintaining legal compliance and safeguarding
public health
 
Presently the
Facilities Management team provide planned and reactive maintenance
services for the Council's land and property either directly or on
behalf of the Council's service areas. In addition, the Council is
implementing a Corporate Landlord Model, whereby ultimately this
team will be responsible for the maintenance of Council owned land
and buildings in the future, excepting schools, which have
differing management arrangements. The Council's property portfolio
is comprised of a mixture of operational and non-operational
assets, ranging from offices and publicly accessed venues,
commercial and retail properties and assets held for regeneration
and schools.
 
The Council has a
statutory duty to ensure that its assets comply the Health and
Safety at Work etc Act 1974 and associated Regulations.
 
The award of the new
water hygiene monitoring and risk assessment contract will ensure
the Council can fulfil its statutory obligations to ensure that all
its assets comply with relevant Health and Safety legislation and
regulations. Failure to implement an appropriate solution for water
hygiene monitoring and risk assessment would significantly hinder
the Council’s ability to meet these legal
responsibilities.
 

There is no viable
“do-nothing” option. The Council must have a contract
in place to ensure compliance with its statutory obligations, as
outlined in this report. Under the Health and Safety at Work etc.
Act 1974, the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations
2002 (COSHH), and the Approved Code of Practice L8 –
Legionnaires’ Disease: The Control of Legionella Bacteria in
Water Systems – the Council is legally required to manage and
mitigate risks associated with water systems.
 
The Council could look
to let individual pieces of work on a case-by-case basis. This
would present a significant challenge to administer, significantly
increase the cost of administration and would not be satisfactory
for certain works, for example emergency call out. Not
commissioning would generate significant challenges to the
Facilities Management team, impacting their operational
effectiveness, in provision of works and would have significant
implications for the operation of the Council's property portfolio,
which may lead to asset non availability or Health and Safety
implications.
 
The Council could
explore other options, for example outsourcing models, however
there is a requirement for a contract to be in place now to enable
delivery of works and any development of a proposal for outsourcing
would need to be properly developed, so the best outcome for the
Council could be achieved and the contract mobilised.

The
Assistant Director – Housing Services has approved the award
of a contract for emergency accommodation for homeless people aged
18 to 24 years to Birkenhead Forum Housing Association (Company
Registration Number 
IP19269R) for a two-year contract commencing on
1st June 2026 with the option  to extend for a
further two 12 month periods at a total cost of £458,421
based on a 4-year term.
 

This contract supports
the Council in its duty to assess and accommodate if there is
reason to believe an individual is homeless, eligible for
assistance and in priority need. Those in priority need include,
those leaving care and any young person with significant health
issues that means they are vulnerable.
 
Supported Homeless
Accommodation Services assists people to develop the skills they
need to live independently and forms a crucial pathway for people,
preventing homelessness and promoting independence. Such services
significantly reduce levels of repeat homelessness and tenancy
failure, thereby generating financial savings across several budget
streams.
 
The
commissioning of an emergency accommodation scheme for young people
directly supports the objectives of the Council’s
Homelessness & Rough Sleeping Strategy 2025–2030 by
providing safe, stable accommodation combined with targeted support
for some of the borough’s most vulnerable residents. The
service contributes to the Council’s ambition to prevent
homelessness, reduce rough sleeping, and support people to move
away from crisis and towards sustained independence.
 
This procurement
exercise was conducted in accordance with the Authority’s
Contract Standing Orders for below?threshold contracts and the
principles of transparency, proportionality, equal treatment, and
value for money.
 
A below?threshold
Light Touch Process was adopted, which is permitted under the
Contract Standing Orders where the nature of the services and
contract value allow flexibility in approach while maintaining
appropriate competition. Five suitably qualified providers were
invited to tender, satisfying the requirement to seek competition
wherever practicable.
 
At tender close, one
compliant tender was received. The tender was fully evaluated
against the published criteria and assessed as offering value for
money. The evaluation confirmed that the bidder meets the
Authority’s requirements and has the capacity and capability
to deliver the services.
 
Appendix 1 sets out
the details of the tenders received.

The information in Appendix 1 is commercially sensitive and is
restricted by virtue of Paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Schedule 12A of
the Local Government Act 1972 as it is ‘Information relating
to the financial or business affairs of any particular person (including the authority holding
the information).

Do nothing: Discounted
as the Council has a duty to assess and accommodate if there is
reason to believe an individual is homeless under Housing Law.
 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.
 
Background
Papers
 
Wirral Homelessness & Rough Sleeping
Strategy 2020-2025

The Assistant Director
of Property and Investment has approved that Scheidt & Bachmann
(UK) Ltd (Company Number 03805576) be directly awarded a contract
to the value of £131,749 via the ESPO Framework 509_23
Parking Management Solutions; Lot 2 – Pay on Foot Solutions
to undertake the replacement of Car Parking Equipment at the
Pyramids Car Park, Borough Road and The Grange Car Park, Conway
Street.

The decision is
required because the existing parking equipment at both car parks
is failing, approaching the end of its economic life, and
generating frequent operational issues that place income at
significant risk.  Jones Lang LaSalle
Limited (JLL), the property management company responsible for the
management of the car parks, has undertaken a detailed site review
and has recommended instructing Scheidt & Bachmann, the
incumbent operator who has full knowledge of both sites.
 
There have been delays
in progressing the recommendation and continued delay would risk
losing card?payment capability altogether, which currently
represents around 50% of all income. 
The equipment does not meet current Banking Clearing standards,
meaning card transaction support could cease at any time and card
payments would no longer be accepted, severely reducing revenue and
increasing operational disruption.
 
Replacing the system
now, via direct award, will protect annual income of £356,555
and more than £1.78 million over five years (based on 2025
figures), while also reducing running costs by at least
£48,000 over the same period. Continued system failures at
The Grange (Conway Street) car park already result in barriers
being lifted and daily revenue lost. The proposed expenditure is
£131,749, excluding operational and licensing costs which are
existing obligations and not part of the replacement cost.
Replacement is therefore essential to secure financial stability,
maintain service continuity, and safeguard critical income streams
for Wirral Borough Council.
 
The award will be
supported by a formal contract, which will be prepared by the
Council’s legal team in due course.
 
The decision made
accords with the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules and the
Public Contract Regulations 2015.

Continuing with the
existing equipment is not a viable option due to repeated failures,
rising maintenance challenges, and the imminent loss of card
payment capability, which would significantly reduce
revenue. 
 
Sourcing alternative
providers to S&B via a full competitive process would introduce
further delays at a point where system failure presents an
immediate risk to income generation and functionality.
 
Another alternative
was for the Council to internally resource the oversight of the
project. Given current capacity constraints, JLL’s Building
Consultancy team has confirmed they can provide project management
services if required, ensuring continuity, technical knowledge, and
delivery at pace. 
 
A further option
considered was delaying replacement until wider strategic decisions
on car park management are made. 
However, this was discounted due to the severe and immediate
financial risk associated with ongoing equipment failure and loss
of payment functionality.
 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.
 
Background
Papers
 
Quotation
JLL Recommendation
Council’s Contract Procedure Rules and
the Public Contract Regulations 2015

The Assistant Director
of Housing Services has approved the purchase of the property
listed in the exempt appendix 1 with an estimated acquisition cost
of £135,000

Successive governments
have recognised that Local Authorities such as Wirral Borough
Council which have welcomed Ukrainian and Afghan arrivals, continue
to face challenges in securing settled accommodation for these
households, which unless alleviated will further impact on existing
housing pressures.
 
In December 2022, the
Local Authority Housing Fund (LAHF) was launched, providing Local
Authorities successful in securing funding, 40% of the total costs
to secure properties for both this purpose and to support councils
in increasing their temporary accommodation for homelessness
pressures.
Wirral Council has
been allocated a total of £648,140.89 in the fourth round of
Local Authority Housing Funding (LAHF4), announced in November 2025
for the rapid acquisition of six properties. The objectives of the
LAHF 4 programme are to:
 
a) Reduce local
housing pressures and use of expensive and unsuitable
accommodation, by providing better quality temporary accommodation
to those owed homelessness duties by local authorities.
 
b) Provide sustainable
settled housing for some families on the Afghan Resettlement
Programme (ARP) so that they can build new lives in the UK, find
employment and integrate into communities.
 
c) Support local
housing markets by assisting the delivery of new housing stock or
new developments to grow overall housing supply
 
The LAHF4 allocation
offered provides 40% of the total costs of five property
acquisitions and 50% for one larger property acquisition. The
required match funding of £721,000 is being provided through
the existing National Resettlement Pathway Programme revenue
funding along with Asylum Dispersal Grant already received by
Wirral Council.
 
Of the six properties
three must be for Afghan resettlement and three for use as
temporary accommodation.
 
Officers from
Strategic Housing Services and the Asset Management Team are
continuing to work collectively to identify suitable properties to
purchase utilising this funding.
 
Costs associated with
compliance checks and any essential repairs required to the
properties will also be met from this funding.
 
A first property has
now been identified (details in appendix 1) to purchase under LAHF
4, with the agreed purchase price of £135,000 (excluding
associated costs which will also be met from this funding).
 
The Total number of
properties acquired under the overall LAHF programme to date is 24
with a further 4 progressing through the conveyancing process.
 
Property acquisition
details are set out in the attached exempt appendix 1.  Appendix 1 is exempt from
publication pursuant to paragraph 3 of the part 1 of Schedule
12 A of the Local Government Act 1972 (Information relating to the
financial or business affairs of any particular person (including
the authority holding that information) because it contains or
refers to information relating to the financial and business
affairs of the Council and the public interest in maintaining the
exemption outweighs the public interest in disclosure.

The Council could have
given this grant funding to Registered Providers to acquire
additional housing stock in the borough, but the preferred option
is to acquire the properties for Council Ownership so that an
income can be generated in the future from rental income and reduce
the burden on housing subsidy loss for use of bed and
breakfast.
 
The Council already
has an existing management agreement in place with a local
Registered Provider of Affordable housing in relation to its small
social housing stock base and these homes can be added to this
agreement without the need to procure a further partner.

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

The Assistant Director
– Housing Services has decided to directly award a new
contract commencing on 1st May 2026 and expiring on 30th
April 2027 for direct access supported housing services for people
aged from 25 years to Riverside Group Ltd (Company registration
number IP030938) with a contract value of £217,000.00.
 

Supported Homeless
Accommodation Services assists people to develop the skills they
need to live independently and forms a crucial pathway for people,
preventing homelessness and promoting independence. It
significantly reduces levels of repeat homelessness and tenancy
failure, thereby generating financial savings across several budget
streams.
 
Riverside Group
Limited is the incumbent supplier of a Direct Access Supported
Housing service for homeless people aged from 25 years and has held
this contract since 2023 when it was originally procured through a
competitive tender exercise.
 
The contract was let
on a 1+1+1 year basis and all remaining options to extend have been
taken.
 
During 2025, the
statutory 5-year review of homelessness within the borough took
place. This process explores the likely future demand for homeless
accommodation services. The review identified that there is a
cohort of homeless people that present with additional complex
issues, including unresolved mental health problems and social care
needs for whom the current level of service provision may not be
suitable.
 
Informed by the
findings of this review, the Council’s Homelessness and Rough
Sleeping Strategy 2025/30, endorsed by the Council’s Economy,
Regeneration and Housing Committee on 16 December 2025, commits to
establishing a joint working group across Housing, Adult Social
Care and Public Health departments to explore the feasibility of
co-commissioning a homeless supported housing service for people
with high levels of health and/or care needs.
 
Given this, it has
been determined appropriate to award Riverside Group Limited a new
12-month contract in respect of Direct Access Supported Housing to
ensure continuation of service to vulnerable, homeless people while
the Council explores the potential for co-commissioning homeless
accommodation services with other departments.
 
The direct award
contract, which is the subject matter of this decision, will begin
on 1st May 2026 and is due to expire on 30th
April 2027. The value of the contract for this period is
£217,000.00 which will be met through the Supported Housing
Programme budget.

 
The Assistant Director -
Procurement  is content that this
decision can be authorised under the 
Council’s Contract Procedure Rules (Rule 12.4.1(b)) as a
lawful, value?for?money exception.
 


Recommission Direct
Access Supported Housing in its current form, let on a 1+1+1
basis.  This has been disregarded based
on the Wirral Homelessness & Rough Sleeping Strategy 2025/30,
Priority 4: Work in partnership to meet housing, health and care
needs.  It is anticipated Housing,
Public Health and Adult Social Care need time to explore the
feasibility of co-commissioning supported housing provision that
will also safely meet the needs of those who present with high
levels of health and social care need. 

 

Putting the contract
out to tender for a 12 month period places a high level of burden
on bidders for a short period of funding.  This has been discounted.

 

The alternative
option was to have allowed the previous contract to naturally
expire and not recommission. This was discounted as it would leave
the council without a key contributing resource to meet its
obligations under Housing Law.

 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.
 
Background
Papers
 
Wirral Homelessness & Rough
Sleeping Strategy 2025/30

Pensions is requested to approve the appointment of a supplier for
an integrated Pensions Administration & Pensioner Payroll
System, following a framework procurement and under delegated
authority from Pensions Committee on 23 June 2025. The contract
term is for ten years – an initial five years with the option
to extend for a further five years.

The
Director of Pensions has approved the appointment of Heywood
Limited as the supplier for an initial period of five years, with
an option for a five-year extension, in annual increments as the
‘Most Economically Advantageous Tenderer’ following a
mini competition conducted via the National Local Government
Pension Scheme Framework at estimated
ten-year cost of £11,557,235.
 

The provision of a
Pensions Administration System is essential for the delivery of the
statutory functions of the Local Government Pension Scheme.

The provision of a
Pensions Administration System is essential for the delivery of the
statutory functions of the Local Government Pensions
Scheme.  Not awarding a contract for the
period from 1 January 2027, would mean that the administering
authority would be sanctioned by the Ministry of Housing and Local
Government and the Pensions Regulator as failing to meet its
obligations to 153,000+ Scheme members.
 
Given the value of the
contract, a full market procurement was deemed to be resource
intensive and given the niche market for local government pensions
administration systems there were many advantages to taking a
further competition route pursuant to the National Local Government
Pensions Scheme (LGPS) Framework for Pensions Administration
Software. These advantages included, shortened timescales, reduced
procurement and legal costs, a minimum specification of
functionality and agreed Terms & Conditions of contract with
the system providers.

content:
This report seeks approval for
a 12 month direct award to Sanctuary Care Limited for the continued
delivery of the Tollemache Road Short Breaks (Respite) Service at a
cost of £637,759, ensuring continuity of essential Short
Breaks provision while the Council completes the full
recommissioning of the Learning Disability and Autism Short Breaks
offer for implementation from November 2026 onwards.
 

The
Director of Adults, Health and Strategic Commissioning
has:
 
1.  approved the direct award
of a 12 month contract to Sanctuary Care Limited for the Tollemache
Road Short Breaks Service, with an estimated contract value of
£637,759; and
 
2.  deemed the above decision
urgent and not subject to the procedure for re
consideration.
 
 

Short
breaks provide statutory and essential support for carers, families
and the people they care for. They safeguard the resilience of care
arrangements, prevent carer fatigue, and support families to
maintain their caring role safely. The Care Act 2014 places duties
on the Council to ensure sufficient preventative and carer?support
services are available.
 
On 18
July 2024 the Adult Social Care and Public Health Committee
approved a full review and recommissioning of the Learning
Disability and Autism short breaks offer. Since then, extensive review and re
design activity has been underway through the Council’s
commissioning programme, ensuring that services remain effective,
efficient, high quality and financially sustainable
 
The
current short breaks offer at Tollemache Road needs to remain
operational during this period to prevent service disruption and to
ensure continuity for families who rely on regular, planned
respite. A direct award is therefore necessary to maintain
stability while the new model is finalised and procured.
 
The
direct award creates the essential time needed to develop a new
Short Breaks Framework, which will broaden the offer beyond a
single residential service. This aligns with what families told the
Council they want which is a more personalised, flexible set of
options alongside a residential facility.
 
Families and carers may be
anxious about change; therefore, maintaining provision at
Tollemache Road while the new model is finalised provides
reassurance and demonstrates the Council’s commitment to
continuity and improvement. The services provided from Tollemache
Road have consistently delivered Good rated care (CQC inspection,
July 2023) and positive family feedback, providing assurance that
continued delivery will maintain safe outcomes until the new model
is implemented.

Option
1 is to do nothing:The Council currently
commissions a Short Breaks offer that expires with effect from 17
April 2026.  Failure to extend and carry
out a procurement exercise will leave those in receipt of this
service without a service. This will not only contravene the
Council’s duties under the Care Act 2014, but this was also
rejected due to the risks to carers and cared for individuals, and
the likelihood of increased unplanned emergency
placements.
 
Option
2 is to retender the service immediately:This
option is not feasible due to the time required for co production,
market engagement, framework design, cost modelling. All these
activities whilst started cannot be completed within the required
timeframe.
 
Option 3 is spot purchasing of alternative beds: This
option would be more expensive because spot purchases are typically
priced at higher marginal rates and not provide the continuity of
care or stability for families. Most cared for individuals who use
Tollemache Road rely on routine, familiarity, and well established
relationships with staff.
topline: The Director of Care and Health has decided to approve a 12-month direct award to Sanctuary Care Limited for the Tollemache Road Short Breaks Service, ensuring continuity of essential short breaks provision.

Supported Homeless

streams.
 
Birkenhead Forum
Housing Association Limited (FHA) is the incumbent contractor of a
supported housing service for homeless people with multiple,
complex needs referred to as the ‘Beacon’
Scheme. 
 
In 2020, MHCLG in
conjunction with Homes England announced the ‘Next Steps
Accommodation Project’ (NSAP) and invited bids for funding
from councils working with local providers of homeless
accommodation services to support and enhance service delivery.
 
In partnership with
FHA, the Council submitted a bid for funding that proposed the
enhancement of the delivery of the service provided at the
‘Beacon’ scheme through additional staffing.
 
The bid was successful
and FHA were awarded £52,418 per annum to increase staffing
levels. This funding was originally intended to be awarded for 4
years but has since continued to be awarded year-on-year by Homes
England. FHA were paid this funding directly from Homes
England.
 
This has had an impact
on the Council’s obligations under procurement legislation
insofar as the funding awarded to FHA, which significantly enhances
service delivery, was not transferable to other organisations.
Consequently, an exception from competitive tendering for this
service provision has been sought since 2020, on the basis that a
procurement exercise would result in additional costs to the
council. This has been agreed with both Procurement and Legal
colleagues.
 
However, as of April
2026, all NSAP funding that was previously administered by Homes
England and/or MHCLG has now been transferred to the respective
Councils for administration.
 
As such, now that the
Council holds this funding, it can now tender for this service.
 
The direct award
contract, which is the subject matter of this decision, will begin
on the 1st of April 2026 and is due to expire on
31st December 2026 and will allow for the conclusion of
a tendering exercise.
 
The value of the
contract for this period is £157,713.19 which is in-line with
current contract value and which will be met through the Supported
Housing Programme budget.

- Procurement is content that this decision can be authorised under
the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules (Rule 12.4.1(b)) as a
lawful, value for money exception.

not recommission. This was discounted as this would leave the
council without a key contributing resource to meet its obligations
under Housing Law.

The Assistant Director
– Housing Services has decided to directly award a new
contract commencing on 1st May 2026 and expiring on 30th
April 2027 for homeless supported housing to Birkenhead Young
Men’s Christian Association (company registration number
02534811) with a contract value of £487,828
 

Supported Homeless
Accommodation Services assist people to develop the skills they
need to live independently and forms a crucial pathway for people,
preventing homelessness and promoting independence. It
significantly reduces levels of repeat homelessness and tenancy
failure, thereby generating financial savings across several budget
streams.
 
 Birkenhead Young Men’s Christian Association
(“YMCA Wirral”) is the incumbent supplier of a Direct
Access Supported Housing service for homeless people aged from 18
years and has held this contract since 2023 when it was originally
procured through a competitive tender exercise.
 
The contract was let
on a 1+1+1 year basis and all remaining options to extend have been
taken.
 
During 2025, the
statutory 5-year review of homelessness within the borough took
place. This process explores the likely future demand for homeless
accommodation services. The review identified that there is a
cohort of homeless people that present with additional complex
issues, including unresolved mental health problems and social care
needs for whom the current level of service provision may not be
suitable.
 
Informed by the
findings of this review, the Council’s Homelessness and Rough
Sleeping Strategy 2025/30, endorsed by the Council’s Economy,
Regeneration and Housing Committee on 16 December 2025, commits to
establishing a joint working group across Housing, Adult Social
Care and Public Health departments to explore the feasibility of
co-commissioning a homeless supported housing service for people
with high levels of health and/or care needs.
 
Given this, it has
been determined appropriate to award YMCA Wirral a new 12-month
contract in respect of Direct Access Supported Housing to ensure
continuation of service to vulnerable, homeless people while the
Council explores the potential for co-commissioning homeless
accommodation services with other departments.
 
The direct award
contract, which is the subject matter of this decision, will begin
on 1st May 2026 and is due to expire on 30th
April 2027. The value of the contract for this period is
£487,828 which will be met through the Supported Housing
Programme budget.

 
 The Assistant
Director - Procurement is content that this decision can be
authorised under the Council’s
Contract Procedure Rules (Rule 12.4.1(b)) as a lawful,
value?for?money exception.
 


Recommission Direct
Access Supported Housing in its current form, let on a 1+1+1
basis.  This has been disregarded based
on the Wirral Homelessness & Rough Sleeping Strategy 2025/30,
Priority 4: Work in partnership to meet housing, health and care
needs.  It is anticipated Housing,
Public Health and Adult Social Care need time to explore the
feasibility of co-commissioning supported housing provision that
will also safely meet the needs of those who present with high
levels of health and social care need. 

 

Putting the contract
out to tender for a 12-month period places a high level of burden
on bidders for a short period of funding.  This has been discounted.

 

The alternative
option was to have allowed the previous contract to naturally
expire and not recommission. This was discounted as it would leave
the council without a key contributing resource to meet its
obligations under Housing Law.

 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Assistant Director is satisfied
that paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

The Director of
Neighbourhoods has approved:
 
(1) 
The appointment of Liam Kelly as independent chair for the Central
Birkenhead Pride in Place Neighbourhood Board;
 
(2) 
The appointment of Nicola Fenton as independent chair for the
Seacombe Pride in Place Neighbourhood Board; and
 
(3) 
The appointment of Jennifer Allinson as independent chair for the
Woodchurch Pride in Place Neighbourhood Board.
 

In line with Ministry
of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) guidance
relating to the Pride in Place programme the Council has set out to
undertake an open recruitment process with a view to appointing to
the role of independent Chair for each of the three Pride in Place
Neighbourhood Boards. This is in accordance with the process
approved by the Assistant Director – Regeneration
Officer.  The recruitment process and
evaluation of applications have now been completed.
 
The MHCLG guidance
sets out that the relevant MP will make a recommendation to the
Council for the nomination for Chair in their respective areas.
 
Following the open
recruitment process and the review and evaluation of applications,
the Council has received a nomination of Chair for each of the
three areas from their respective MPs. Following satisfactory due
diligence checks the Director of Neighbourhoods is content to
accept the recommendations and make the appointments. 
 

The alternative option
is to do nothing. In this case an independent chair would not be
appointed, the Neighbourhood Board would not be set up, and the
funding offered through the Price in Place programme could not be
drawn down and spent for the benefit of local communities. This
option has been discounted.
 

The decision has been
taken under Part 3 Section C - Overview and Scheme of Delegations
of Authority to Officers as the decision is not reserved to a
Committee or Sub-Committee and the Director is satisfied that
paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c) apply.

programme launched on 25th September with guidance
released on 3rd December. The prospectus and supporting
documents produced by MHCLG can be found here: 
Pride in Place Programme prospectus - GOV.UK

Notice taken by the Assistant Director: Chief Regeneration Officer
on 23 January 2026 approving the recruitment process can be found
here.  Decision
